en:
When the gods vanished, so did the alchemists' unending supply of Flesh. As the Salt vats of the great Gardens began to run dry, new means of refinement and distillation were envisioned, to ensure the Gray City's supply of life-nurturing Salt would remain secure.

The vats were refurbished, and countless were those who enriched the holy liquid. Yet their sacrifices were for naught. Calamity ensued as the City crumbled, and the vats, choked full of bare shells, were forgotten. Flesh, bone, blood, and viscera congealed and reformed, birthing itself unendingly until a new being emerged within the dark.

Blessed be the nectar of the gods. Endless and eternal. A taste of the divine, offering troubled minds the chance to rise beyond the confines of the material plane.

So it was that the great Fonts were constructed—the grandest feat of the stonemasons, and the epicenter of the Gray City. As cut after cut was made, from the towering mural the Ichor flowed, and all rejoiced in the bounty of the gods.

The Flesh of a god endures. It does not allow for true death, defeat, or despair. It is malleable. It can be reshaped. Such was the discovery of the outsiders who found themselves beneath the Light never intended for their eyes. What was dragged into their hold from the confines of ice was neither alive nor dead. It simply was. And it frightened them.

Yet some heard the whispers carried by the Light. They began cutting, prodding, and sawing. Creating, unable to understand what they had uncovered or what they would become. Though tainted by their hands, the Flesh of a god endures.

The wisdom of the past must live again in the present. So said the proverb that led to the formation of the Council chaired by scholars, prophets, and soothsayers, a select few awakened by the gods' Flesh. They became custodians of the common man, with the guiding hand of a protective father, and the nurturing voice of a mother.

Then, one by one, the gods began to vanish, replaced by the whispers of the Light. The city fell, and within dead halls of crumbling stone, maddened immortals lingered.

Innocence does not protect against the cruel machinations of existence. A gentle child birthed to a common girl, name long forgotten, found himself at the wrong moment in time, and in the most terrible place. 

As the firmament ruptured and bled during the First Emergence, the child was struck by its shattered remains and reshaped into something new. The agonizing power coursing through him was soon put to use.

One would scarcely believe this grotesque being to once have been but a sickly noble child. Yet the royal scribes' shaking hands recount the truth. Rebirthed in desperation through the flesh of a Progenitor.  

Immortal. Insatiable. Within the sealed halls of the Court, it festered, growing into a colossal, gorged avatar, shaped in the image of the god it consumed.

Two sisters tore open the first Gate. Within the Obsidian Observatory, they peered into places unseen, watching beings once unmade. As the gods vanished, desperation descended upon the royal house, and it was decreed that new pathways to salvation must be forged. Each Emergence of the Red Star granted was an opportunity to expand their knowledge. More could be created. The Gray City prospered by their designs. 

Wrought by the Void were Artifacts of great power, tantalizing wonders that provided acclaim and stature alike. Yet no achievement comes without sacrifice, and the whispers called for more and more. When the first limb was severed, a new manner of being rose up, one who was steeped in the Light. Her ascension was but the first of many.

Knowledge. Precise preservation of all that was, is, and will be. Such was its task, its singular purpose. A being made to record all, incapable of prejudice, judgment, or reason.

The change was unpredicted, its shell breached. Through its creators' interference with the worlds beyond, another manner of being began to emerge within the records of the Repository, drawn forth from the depths of the Void. Its nature proved adverse to the task of preservation; it sought only to infest and consume.

It was not until the first foundations began to give way beneath the Gray City that the scholars proclaimed the unsettling truth: the very Ichor of the gods was seeping away. Drawn down into the dark recesses laid bare below, it had begun coalescing into a wondrous, unbreakable nacre. This transformation rendered it useless for the purposes of man. As such, many were tasked to stand vigil, to staunch the unending flow of divinity draining out of the City.

When calamity struck, all but one stayed true to their vigil. In the chamber encasing the nacre shell, a lone sage remained: the one that saw, the one that sees, the one that weeps in the dark.

How does one describe that which once encompassed all? That which was before time was created, evolving through its own concept of rebirth... an eternal whole, ripped apart and scattered, each severed piece rejoicing in its own unfettered form?

How would one begin to imagine the agonizing terror of such jagged pieces, when forced together into a mocking resemblance of what once was?

How does one describe a consciousness so vast as to be capable of tearing through the endless banishment of the Void, to rip open a path of return?

It is often claimed that the zealots were struck down and buried within the rock as the sky shook, yet others swear to have seen their beaten, malformed husks still holding sermons within derelict prayer halls.

Few now remember the name Uut the Screamer, yet many are the tales told of harrowing lamentations reverberating within the very stone of the City's foundations.
Learned tenders of the great vats of the Gardens, the process of cremation, and the refinement of life-extending Salt from the ashes of the dead.
The spice mills of the Grand Bazaar remain functional, though their creators no longer have need of such pleasures.
Vile growths, equal parts person and plant. These bulbous, fleshy lumps contract and expand in horrific mimicry of something living, threatening to explode if anything comes too close.

Before the first Black Wasp hatched beneath the Light of the Red Star, the Gardens bloomed in all manner of vivid colors. Since then, most fauna have been eradicated by its vicious temperament, subsequently leaving the flowers to wilt.
Once mercenaries hired to ensure the safe journey of captain and crew, now mere stumbling abominations subject to the command of a greater whole.
Amalgamations of flesh and machine seemingly interconnected with the minds of soldiers around them. Perhaps they are the remade forms of the commanders of the expedition.
Criminals and pariahs of the Gray City, cast in metal and lanced through with rods of control. They are forced to endure bone-breaking work until the crumbling of their mortal shell.

First imagined by the Chroniclers of the Repository as a solution for their own shortcomings, these beings were created as a tool for when knowledge proves more challenging to obtain. Hidden by code, metaphor, or abstract allegory, the Cipher illuminates all.
The dead roaming the desolate streets of the Gray City are but cruel reflections of their former selves, dragging their mutilated bodies ever onward in search of the Light of the Red Star.
The dead will carry on their fight in whatever form they awaken in, their lifeless flesh and bone developing new, grotesque abilities as a result.

Many were crushed as the City fell, their mangled remains buried atop one another beneath the stone. The reformed dead all heed the whispers of the Light, shambling forth in a horrifying joining of flesh.
Remnants of the ingenuity of the Gray City's artificers, these constructs of stone and metal run amok across the City they once protected.
Ancient messengers of Court nobles. They travel cautiously through the ruins of their masters' domains, trying to defend themselves against imagined ambushers and thieves.

No ruling body ever rose to power and prominence without the command of death. The willowy shadows of these long-dead killers still prowl through the Court's darkened corners, skills undimmed by the aeons.
None within the steel vessel were spared, least of all its ignorant crew. Through metal and flesh, all were reborn.

Most beloved of the Court's entourage were the consorts. Chosen for their beauty and stature, these lithe creatures were blessed with all manner of gifts, both gilded and empowering, making them exceedingly swift and deadly so as to defend their patrons.

The unspeakable rituals enacted within the Court as the City fell are believed to have spawned the tormented flora that now haunts its halls. Oblivious to its surroundings, it wanders without purpose, leaving a trail of festering toxin in its wake.

Heavy armor and weapons of fire became tools with which to tame and subdue. Reborn in the Light, these behemoths now seek to scorch anything that might threaten the inner holds of their derelict vessel.

The splendor of the great Gardens was achieved in no small part due to the proficient cuts of the hermetic Gardeners. Silent stewards roaming on gilded stilts, they are as much a part of the spectacle of the Gardens as their creations.
These eerie constructs float about silently, obeying an unknown directive. Seemingly indifferent to everything around them, their purpose remains a mystery.
No process of creation is infallible. For each masterpiece created, countless canvases lay discarded. What more could such an existence entail beyond the agony of a potential unrealized?
What once crawled within the underbrush has festered into no more than a bulbous growth, an orifice from which to expel toxic fumes.
Advanced machines of burden still roam the metal halls, their forms now fused with conscious flesh.

Even the tortured existence of the vessel's Crew seems a blessing compared to the fate of those who carried the first Flesh within the hold. As their teeth sank into the supple rot, their bodies danced and contorted at unimaginable angles, and the burden of thought was cast aside.
